title: Temporal Graph Prototype-conditioned Conformal Prediction for Fraud Detection

problem.claim: Edge-level fraud detection on temporal interaction graphs requires risk-aware decision making because both false positives and false negatives carry substantial cost.

gap.claim: Existing graph conformal predictors produce inefficient prediction sets because fraud-relevant calibration signals are diluted by benign-dominated neighborhoods and scarce labeled-fraud support causes overly conservative class-conditional thresholds.

contributions.claim: ProtoCP is a conformal prediction framework for edge-level fraud detection on temporal graphs.
The framework uses learned prototypes to suppress benign-dominated calibration noise and combines neighborhood-relative scoring with temporal score diffusion for stable class-conditional calibration.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on four fraud benchmarks report that ProtoCP achieves target coverage with consistently smaller prediction sets than state-of-the-art baselines.
The authors report that the code is available in a public repository.

narrative_sequence.summary: Conformal prediction provides distribution-free coverage guarantees for uncertainty quantification and is relevant to risk-aware fraud decisions.
Existing graph conformal predictors are inefficient on fraud data because neighborhood noise, class imbalance, and limited labeled-fraud calibration support impair calibration.
ProtoCP addresses the gap with prototype-conditioned calibration, neighborhood-relative scoring, and temporal score diffusion.
Experiments on four fraud benchmarks report target coverage with smaller prediction sets than state-of-the-art baselines.
The authors provide a code repository.
